statement: Consider the statement: "Every number in the list that is greater than 10 is even." For which list is the statement false?

choices.misconception: I read the statement backwards, as also saying every even number is greater than 10, and 2 and 4 break that.
I thought a list with no numbers above 10 makes the statement false, because nothing in it supports the claim.
I saw the odd number 9 and forgot the statement only talks about numbers greater than 10.
I thought "every" meant every number in the list must be greater than 10, and 1 is not.

hints: Which numbers does the statement say anything about?
The statement only makes a promise about numbers greater than 10. It is false exactly when the list contains a number greater than 10 that is not even. Numbers 10 or smaller cannot break it.
Look in each list for a number above 10 that is odd.

solutions.reliable: The statement promises that any number above 10 is even. It is broken only by a number above 10 that is odd. The lists contain 12, 14, 20, 30 and 11 above 10, and only 11 is odd, so the list 11, 4, 6 makes it false. The list 3, 5, 7 has nothing above 10, so the promise is never tested and the statement is true. The transferable idea: an if-then statement can only be broken by a case where the if-part holds and the then-part fails.

whyOnTest: Kangaroo logic questions turn on what a statement does and does not claim, including statements that are true because nothing tests them.
